expected.title: Existence and minimal-coupling uniqueness of the Markov-quantile law for arbitrary real-line probability marginals
expected.author: Charles Boubel; Nicolas Juillet
expected.difficulty_reason: Kolmogorov extension does not itself supply transition kernels that are simultaneously Markov-consistent and minimal among increasing-kernel couplings. The authors construct the monotone supremum on quantile levels and prove convergence and compatibility using a contraction metric on fixed-marginal couplings. The separate product-coupling induction establishes minimality and uniqueness without introducing temporal regularity assumptions.

expected.title: A single nested sequence of finite Markovization times approximates the Markov-quantile process
expected.author: Charles Boubel; Nicolas Juillet
expected.difficulty_reason: The new counted claim requires one sequence of finite Markovization sets to work for an uncountable time family without continuity or non-atomicity assumptions. Individual pairwise compactness and the previously examined ordinary concatenation continuity do not suffice. The proof combines monotone level-kernel completion and a common countable diagonal selection with an atomic covariance criterion ensuring that quantile pushforward preserves the necessary finite-chain factorization even at omitted times. These mechanisms supply a substantive research-level simultaneous process construction, beyond the old existence/minimal-pair-coupling theorem and beyond the low-difficulty continuity lemma.

expected.title: A Chebyshev-type integral inequality for positive bounded increasing functions, with equality only for constants
expected.author: Charles Boubel; Nicolas Juillet
expected.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 4.17 at source lines 1905-1912: for a < b and positive bounded increasing functions f, g on the interval, the mean of f g is at least the product of the means, with equality if and only if f or g is constant. The author's proof (source lines 1914-1920) has two parts of different character: the inequality is obtained by constructing two measures of equal mass and showing that one dominates the other through an explicit computation of their cumulative distribution functions, which uses monotonicity of f (line 1916), and then integrating the increasing function g against the dominating measure; the equality analysis is a separate argument that reduces to indicators of intervals [c,b], shows that equality forces c to be an endpoint unless f is constant, and extends the conclusion to positive combinations and then to limits (line 1918). The statement records the inequality and the equality case but neither the comparison of measures nor the reduction to indicators.

expected.title: The action of a finite family of increasing kernels preserves the stochastic order and stabilises the decreasing-density class
expected.author: Charles Boubel; Nicolas Juillet
expected.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 4.4 at source lines 1519-1530: for a finite set R and measures mu, nu in a class of measures, if mu <= nu then mu applied to the kernel l_R is again <= nu applied to it, and if mu has decreasing density then so does mu applied to l_R with mu <= that measure. The author's proof (source lines 1532-1533) is short but contains two different arguments: the first assertion and the first half of the second are reduced to the elementary kernels l_r, for which increase and stabilisation are checked directly (line 1532), while the inequality mu <= mu applied to l_R is proved by passing to cumulative distribution functions, noting that they agree off the components of A_r and that on each component one is affine and the other concave precisely because mu has decreasing density (line 1533). The statement is a two-part lemma about kernels and records neither the reduction to the l_r nor the concavity argument.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of Lemma 4.4, retained line for line

expected.title: The concatenation of transport plans collapses exactly when one kernel is constant on each atom interval
expected.author: Charles Boubel; Nicolas Juillet
expected.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1922-1938, original Lemma 4.18: for a measure with quantile function g and atoms b_i with the intervals A_i they merge, the concatenation of the coupling with the two transport plans equals the plain composition exactly when on each A_i at least one of the two kernel functions is constant, and under that same hypothesis an identity holds for the compositions with measurable maps. The proof (source lines 1940-1967) is a disintegration computation that the statement hides entirely: the concatenation is rewritten through its numbered expression, the difference of the two plans is reduced to a sum of integrals over the atom intervals, and the sign of each summand is decided by the integral inequality for increasing functions, which is also what converts the equality case into the constancy condition; the second assertion repeats the computation under that condition.
